did.abstract: The Osborn Manuscript Files contain single, unbound manuscripts and small groups of manuscripts acquired for the Osborn Collection from various sources at various times.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Manuscripts acquired by gift or purchase from various sources. For further information, consult the curator.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The Osborn Manuscript Files are the physical property of the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University. Literary rights, including copyright, belong to the authors or their legal heirs and assigns. For further information, consult the curator.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: [Author], [Title]. James Marshall and Marie-Louise Osborn Collection, Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: The materials are open for research.
Restricted Fragile Papers may only be consulted with permission of the appropriate curator. Preservation photocopies for reference use have been substituted in the main files.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Bibliographic descriptions for OSB MSS FILE # 1-16601 were converted into online lists from previously existing card sets in the Manuscript Catalog. All pertinent bibliographic information on the cards has been retained. OSB MSS FILE # 16601 and higher were cataloged directly into online lists, arranged in order as cataloged.
Additions to this archival collection ceased with OSB MSS File # 19598. Subsequent OSB MSS FILES are cataloged individually in the library's online catalog.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Osborn Manuscript Files contain single, unbound manuscripts and small groups of manuscripts acquired for the Osborn Collection which the Library has chosen to describe in finding-aid style lists rather than as discrete entries in Yale University Library's on-line public access catalog (ORBIS). The materials in the Osborn Manuscript Files include literary and historical manuscripts, individual and small groups of letters, and single documents, as well as some "Unprocessed" material such as engraved portraits and bibliographic information.
Materials described in the Osborn Manuscript Files lists are grouped as follows:
OSB MSS FILE # 1 - 16660 are arranged alphabetically under headings for author or other closely related personal or corporate name. Items of unidentified authorship are listed by title or topic.
OSB MSS FILE # 16601 - 19598 are listed in the order described.

OSB MSS FILE # 19599 and above, as well as other materials in the Osborn Collection, including archival collections and manuscripts in bound format, are cataloged separately and can be found in the online catalog.

Collection of letters and documents
from her papers, concerning her
affairs after the death of
her father, Charles Edward,
the Young Pretender.
Collection includes:
LS from Armand Marc, Comte de
Montmorin de Saint Herem
to the Duchess concerning her pension.
A list of the letters and papers
belonging to the House of Stuart
deposited at the English
Benedictine monastery in Paris,
signed by William Cowley. List of
silver plate received from the Duchess
by the silversmith Tomaso Zapporti.
Document concerning rents granted
to the Duchess by Henry Cardinal
York. Calculation of the income and
expenses of the Duchess and her
household, with a list of pensions
payable under Charles Edward's will.
A copy of her will, made at Bologna,
1789 Nov 14. Accounts concerning the
Spanish pensions of Cardinal York.

did.unittitle: [Account of the religious conferences between Francis White and John Fisher]: contemporary manuscript

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
66p.
31 cm.
Contents: 1) A coppye of that shortt
wrytten paper wch was the occasion of
the conferrence between D. White ande
me; 2) A relation of what passed in the
first conferrence betwixt D. Whyte
and me; 3) A relation of the second
conferrence...; and 4) A brief relation
of what passed in a third pryvat
conferrence betwixt a Bishopp [Laud]
and me...
These conferences took place in 1622,
at the desire of King James I, before
the Countess of Buckingham, who was
leaning to catholicism. Fisher
defended the catholic aid against
Francis White, afterwards Bishop of
Ely. The King attended the conferences,
the third and last of which was held on
24 May 1622, when Laud replaced White.
Fisher's account of the Conferences was
circulated widely in manuscript (see
volume II of Laud's Works, Oxford, 1849).

obstructed him while governor.

Hastings instructs Duncan, while
pretending to escort treasure to Dacca,
to surprise and "seize the person of
Mahamud Ruffeh...all his family, and
every person who has any concern in
his robberies." He is to keep his
Sepoys from molesting civilians. The
second letter proposes a scheme to trap
a traitorous guide.

did.unittitle: LS (retained copy) to [Lord North], Fort William [Calcutta]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
11 p.
24 x 19 cm.
On the seizure of control at Madras
by Lord Pigot and his subsequent over-
throw from power. Hastings indicates
that the Council in Bengal acted
"instantly and unanimously...to
acknowledge the authority of the new
Government..." and at the same time
explains the absence of any action
taken by him personally. Hastings
views the problems in Madras as
fundamental to the governance of India
and perhaps sympathizes with Pigot.
Makes several detailed suggestions for
changing the power structure. Within
two weeks, however, Col Monson died,
restoring Hastings's dominance in
Bengal.

did.unittitle: Petition to the Commissioners of the Treasury. London.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
1 p., repaired. 30 x 39 cm.
The petitioners state that they
drew up proposals relating to a
considerable discovery of money
and money's worth, but forbore
same on finding that one Madam
Danby had a reference to Mr.
Blathwayt upon her pretence of a
like discovery; they ask that, as
Madam Danby has not proceeded with
her petition for a year, her
petition be set aside. The estates
and moneys referred to in the
petition are in the West Indies.
Endorsed by Henry Guy, secretary
to the treasury, referring both
petitions to the consideration
of Mr. Blathwayt; with Guy's
signature, 1681 Feb 28.
See Cal. Treas. Books 1679-80,
p. 759; 1681-85, pp. 59-60, 63,
126.
Southwell and Blathwayt papers,
no. 8.

did.unittitle: Instructions given to Mr. Anthony Mildmay sent unto Duke Casimir the xjth of July 1578, [Antwerp].

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
4 p.
31 x 21 cm.
Signed by Walsingham and Lord
Cobham. Walsingham and Cobham were
in Antwerp on a special mission
when they sent Mildmay, Walsingham's
nephew, with these instructions to
acquaint Duke John Casimir "sith
the cause of our owne Cominge
hither". The principal cause was
the unwelcome news that the Estates
had invited the Duke of Alencon
and Anjou to come to their aid
against Spain. This document
embodies a detailed summary, drawn
up for Casimir, of the whole course
of the negotiations, both in France
and in the Low Countries.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
Manuscript calling for the defeat

George I in the general election
of 1722. Attacks the German influence
on the English Court; martial law
and the revived standing army; the
undermining of the Established
Church; and the fiscal mismanagement
and corruption of Robert Walpole and
other ministers. Detailed contrasts
are drawn between the "Court Party"
and the "Country Party."
The author devotes three pages to
denunciations of the government's
handling of the Mississippi and
South Seas Bubbles.
Octavo ms. stitched; remains of
black coated paper wrappers.

expresses hope that Macartney will

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents

Furnell, specifying his destination,
possible prizes, rules for taking
prizes, contraband and hostages and
for allowing neutral ships to pass,
directions for account and record

instructions on ship's discipline.
2) Manuscript notes relating to

Lyon's insignia. 3) The accounts
of the winnings from first and

1744 as distributed to the
shareholders, who included Jeremiah
Ames, William Jefferis, Edward
Whatley, Stephen Perry, and Sidenham
Teast. 4) Printed booklet of bills

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
54 ALS from various correspondents
to John Jackson, mostly brief and
of a business or professional nature.
Correspondents include William Davies,
Martha Smith, Nicholas Brown, Mary
Ann Swafford, Edward Paget, Robert
Crosby, and Henrietta Greene.
Subjects include portrait commissions
for Jackson; his memberships in
various societies; Jackson's trip
to Italy with Sir Francis Chantrey,
and a visit by Canova to England.
Other items are brief social notes
confirming appointments and
engagements.
Acc.: 03.1.20

descriptivenote.p: ALS to Sir Richard Southwell

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
Letter from Dering to his uncle
describing a duel he fought with
Captain Henry Goring over a visit
paid by Dering to the actress Mrs.
Barry (Elizabeth Barry, ca.
1658-1713). The duel took place on
June 10, 1685, backstage after
a play (probably the Dorset Garden
Theatre) and resulted in the
death of Goring from "a cut throat."
Dering also discusses the Coroner's
inquest in progress and Sir
Henry Goring's comment that he had
"too great reason to believe that his
son was very much in drink" at the
time.
With: "The severall Informations and
Depositions taken before the Coroners
Inquest the 11th and 18 of June 1685."
Manuscript, also in Dering's hand,
of testimony given by several
witnesses to the duel, including
Mrs. Barry herself and the actors
James Wiltshire and William Mountfort.
From the library of Sir Thomas
Phillipps.
Acc.: 03.1.24

Letters concerning taxes in the parish of St. Martin's-in-the-Fields

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
1) ALS to John Tovey, 1723 Mar 27:
denies that her house in St. James
Park is in the parish of St. Martin's
and declares that no evidence to
the contrary has been produced.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
2) LS to [Zachary Pearce],
1726 Jul 18: sets out her case at
length, citing Acts of Parliament
and surveyor's notes;
Docketed: Ds. of Marlborough's
letter. July 18, 1726.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
3) ALS, draft, corrected, from
Zachary Pearce to the Duchess of
Marlborough; Tunbridge Wells,
1726 Jul 27: lengthy letter
refuting the Duchess' arguments
in detail, citing precedents and
recent legal opinion; hopes to
"prevent a lawsuit or seizure."
Docketed: A Copy of my (struck
out) Dr. Pearce's letter to the
D.ss of Marlborough, July 27, 1726.

did.unittitle: 3 documents concerning the British Army in the Caribbean

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
1) "State of the Garrisons in the
Charibee Islands on the 1 Nov 1794:"
census of officers, rank and file,
and provincials stationed on 10
British Caribbean islands. The
highest totals are for St. Lucia
and "Martinico" (Martinique).
Signed by Sir John Vaughan.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
2) "Royal Artillery in the Charibee
Islands 15th Nov. [17]94."
Signed by Sir John Vaughan.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
3) "State of the Light Dragoons in
the Charibee Islands the 25th
Nov.br 1794."
Signed by J. Hare.

did.unittitle: HANDBILL FOR A FREEHOLD ESTATE SALE
"Advertisement of the Estate to be Sold"

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
Manuscript handbill advertising
a freehold estate at Cranborne
in Dorset, including "a new-built
Brick House elegantly adorned
with Stone," a garden, an
eight-horse stable and 62 acres
of land. Inquiries are to be
directed to Samuel Stillingfleet,
Attorney at Law
Title from docket.

did.unittitle: ALS to [Henry Howard, Earl of Suffolk]; Inverary

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
Lengthy letter to Suffolk (Secretary
of State for the Northern Department)
requesting his support for the Hamilton
candidate for Lanark in the
approaching Parliamentary elections.
She also outlines the troubled history
of the recent elections, in which
the Hamilton family supported the
candidates of the Duke of Douglas
due to "the hazard of doing prejudice
to my son's expectations...in case
of refusal."
